Definition: Kazhdan pairs/sets, displacement constant kappa(G,Q,pi) and Kazhdan constant kappa(G,Q), from KHV Definition 1.1.3 and Remark 1.1.4 (fetched full text, sha256_16 0281823290dfb42e). Checked the two elementary identifications claimed in the item: (Q,eps) is a Kazhdan pair iff kappa(G,Q) >= eps (monotonicity in eps plus the interval structure), and kappa(G,Q,pi) >= kappa(G,Q) for every representation without nonzero invariant vector. Dependency def-almost-invariant-vectors is the only in-run one (level 0); the rest are published.

Definition: property (T) via almost invariant vectors, for topological groups; the compact-Kazhdan-set formulation is delegated to the in-run thm-property-t-is-equivalent-to-the-existence-of-a-kazhdan-pair (level 2). Sources: KHV Definition 1.1.3 and Remark 1.1.2, Breuillard Lecture 2 Sec. II, read in the fetched full texts. All deps published except def-almost-invariant-vectors; the two displayed formulations are definitionally identical.

Lemma: coefficient/displacement identities ||pi(g)xi-xi||^2 = 2(1-Re<pi(g)xi,xi>) and |1-<pi(g)xi,xi>| <= ||pi(g)xi-xi|| (Cauchy-Schwarz), the net indexed by the directed set of pairs (Q,eps) (the only choice input, AC declared), and the GNS converse. Source: KHV Ch. 1 Sec. 1.1 and Appendix F.1 (Corollary F.1.5), Breuillard Lecture 2 Sec. II. Scaffold repair during construction: the GNS converse is stated as net asymptotic invariance together with a Hilbert direct sum, since a single GNS representation need not itself have almost invariant vectors; the strategy records this caveat and adds def-hilbert-direct-sum-of-unitary-representations. Deps are published or the in-run definition.

II and Exercises Sec. 2 I.1 (read in the fetched full texts). Route: direct sum over all pairs (Q,eps) with witnesses (the AC selection) for (i)->(ii), and the orthogonal-projection estimate ||xi-Pxi|| <= delta||xi|| for the quantitative clause. Deps: in-run def-almost-invariant-vectors and def-kazhdan-pair (levels 0-1), otherwise published Hilbert-space and direct-sum suppliers.

Definition: compact generation for locally compact Hausdorff groups (G = union of Q^n for a compact Q), with the elementary examples (compact groups; sigma-compact connected groups). Source: Breuillard Lecture 2 Sec. II and the KHV Theorem 1.3.1 context, read in the fetched full texts. Deps published; no choice principle.

Theorem: (T) implies compact generation (KHV Theorem 1.3.1; Breuillard Lecture 2 Sec. II). Route: direct sum of the quasi-regular representations on the coset spaces G/H over the directed set of open compactly generated subgroups; if G is not compactly generated every G/H is infinite, so the Dirac vectors give almost invariance and no invariant vector, contradicting (T). AC is declared for the subgroup and representative selections. Deps: published items plus the in-run def-compactly-generated-locally-compact-group (level 0).

Theorem: (T) passes to Hausdorff quotients (KHV Theorem 1.3.4). Route: pull a representation of G/N back along the open surjection p; compact images p(Q) witness almost invariance, and invariant vectors transfer because p is surjective; no compactness lifting is used. Deps all published; no additional choice beyond ambient suppliers.

Definition: spectral gap as 1_G not weakly contained in pi restricted to H^G-perp for arbitrary topological groups, with the displacement form (there are compact Q and eps>0 with sup_Q||pi(x)xi-xi|| >= eps||xi|| for all xi in H^G-perp) asserted under the locally compact Hausdorff hypothesis, where the published lem-weak-containment-of-the-trivial-representation-and-almost-invariant-vectors identifies the two; the converse beyond locally compact groups is not claimed, since the published lemma's remark proves it false. Deps published (def-locally-compact-space added with the hypothesis).

Theorem: (T) iff there are one compact Q and eps>0 with the uniform displacement bound over H^G-perp for every strongly continuous unitary representation; proof via the Kazhdan-pair equivalence and the orthogonal projection of a (Q,eps)-invariant unit vector. Identification with spectral gap in the sense of def-spectral-gap-for-a-unitary-representation is stated for locally compact Hausdorff G. Sources: Breuillard Lecture 2 Sec. II, Exercises Sec. 2 I.1; KHV Proposition 1.1.9, read in the fetched full texts. AC declared for the Kazhdan-pair equivalence. Deps published plus in-run levels 0-2.

Lemma: for locally compact Hausdorff G, compactness iff finite Haar volume iff the left regular representation has a nonzero invariant vector iff the constant 1 lies in L^2(G). Source: KHV Remark 1.1.2(vii) and Appendix A.5.1, read in the fetched full text. Route: a nonzero translation-invariant L^2 function has equal positive mass on every translate of a compact set carrying positive mass, so non-compactness forces infinitely many disjoint translates and divergence of the L^2 integral; countable recursion, AC declared and inherited from the Haar-measure chain. Deps published.

Theorem: amenable plus (T) implies compact (KHV Theorem 1.1.6, read in the fetched full text). Route: the in-run Hulanicki criterion (batch 2, level 7) turns amenability into almost invariant vectors of the left regular representation; (T) produces a nonzero invariant vector; the in-run finite-Haar-volume criterion forces compactness. Deliberate deviation from the design's 'isolation of the trivial representation' phrase so that the held isolation theorem is not consumed; recorded in the batch notes. Deps: batch-2 def-amenable (level 1) and thm-hulanicki (level 7), otherwise published.

Theorem: compact Hausdorff groups have (T); (K,eps) is a Kazhdan pair for every 0<eps<=1, witnessed by the Bochner average eta = int_K pi(x)xi dmu(x) with ||eta-xi|| <= sup_K||pi(x)xi-xi|| < 1, hence eta nonzero, and invariance by left invariance of Haar measure (KHV Proposition 1.1.5). AC enters through the normalized Haar probability. Deps published plus in-run defs/theorems at levels 1-2.

Definition: relative property (T) and relative Kazhdan pairs for a pair (G,H), H not assumed normal; H=G reduces to property (T) (KHV Definition 1.4.3 and Remark 1.4.4, read in the fetched full text). No well-definedness obligation is left open; dependencies are published except the in-run def-almost-invariant-vectors.

Definition: P^1(R) as the set of lines in R^2, identified with the one-point compactification R* = R union {infinity}. Compact metrizability is established locally: inverse stereographic projection h(t) = (2t/(t^2+1),(t^2-1)/(t^2+1)), h(infinity)=(0,1), is a continuous bijection from the compact Hausdorff R* onto S^1, hence a homeomorphism (closed subsets of R* are compact, their images compact and so closed in S^1), and the circle metric transports. Scaffold repair: the B-examples-homed published example ex-one-point-compactifications-of-the-line-and-of-the-naturals was dropped because an item may not depend on an item homed only on a B page (validate-plan b-leaf rule); the homeomorphism is now proved locally from A-homed published suppliers (thm-one-point-compactification-properties, lem-unit-circle-is-a-compact-metrizable-topological-group, def-metrizable-space, thm-compactness-under-continuous-maps, thm-compact-subset-of-a-hausdorff-space-is-closed, thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact, thm-heine-borel-r). The SL2(R) action, its well-definedness, the Mobius formula and the unipotent computations were checked. Deps all published and A-homed.

Lemma: no Borel probability on P^1(R) is invariant under two unipotents with distinct fixed lines, in particular u_+ and u_- (Breuillard Exercises Sec. 2 III.5, read in the fetched full text). Proof: in a basis adapted to the fixed lines the unipotents are I+cE_12 and I+c'E_21, acting as t -> t+c (fixing infinity) and s -> s+c' in the charts t=x/y and s=y/x; invariance under the first forces nu = delta_infinity because the sets [kc,(k+1)c) partition R with equal mass, and the second unipotent moves infinity. Deps published plus the in-run def-real-projective-line (level 0).

Lemma: (SL2(R) x| R^2, R^2) has relative (T), with an explicit finite Q_0 and eps_0 in (0,1]. Route: separable G-invariant subspaces; PVM of pi_m restricted to R^2 by the published spectral-measure lemma (N second-countable abelian LCH, separable Hilbert space, K = SL2(R) second countable); identification of the dual of R^2 with R^2 through chi_xi(y)=e^{2 pi i xi.y}, using the published A-homed lem-continuous-characters-of-the-real-line-are-exponentials and lem-duals-of-finite-products-and-discrete-direct-sums (the B-homed ex-pontryagin-dual-of-euclidean-space was dropped under the b-leaf rule); E({0})=0 because there is no nonzero N-invariant vector; pushforward of the spectral probability to P^1(R); the total-variation estimate |mu_{pi(g)xi}(B)-mu_xi(B)| <= 2||pi(g)xi-xi||; extraction of a weakly convergent subsequence (published compact-metric lemma); the limit probability is fixed by the unipotent actions (u_+^{-1})^T and (u_-^{-1})^T, contradicting the projective-line lemma. AC declared for the subsequence and the measure-theoretic choices. Deps: in-run def-real-projective-line and the projective-line lemma (levels 0-1), otherwise published.

Lemma: quantitative form of relative (T): for a relative Kazhdan pair (Q,eps), dist(xi,H^N) <= eps^{-1} sup_Q||pi(q)xi-xi|| and sup_{n in N}||pi(n)xi-xi|| <= 2 eps^{-1} sup_Q||pi(q)xi-xi||, plus the strict form when Q is compact with G = union of Q^k, proved by contradiction with the Hilbert direct sum and telescoping; AC declared for the counterexample choices. Deps: in-run def-relative-property-t-for-a-pair and def-almost-invariant-vectors (levels 0-1), otherwise published Hilbert-space suppliers.

Lemma: for n>=2 every g in SL_n(R) is a product of at most 2n^2+6n elementary transvections; explicit real Gaussian elimination with pivot repair (at stage k at most 2(n-k)+1 transvections, at most n^2-1 in total), the six-transvection factorization diag(a,a^{-1}) = t_+(a) t_-(-a^{-1}) t_+(a) (t_-(1) t_+(-1) t_-(1)) in each 2x2 block (verified by direct multiplication), and inversion. Source: Breuillard Exercises Sec. 2 II.1 (real field only; no integer bounded-generation theorem). Deps all published.
